definitions.explanation: An architectural feature where floors are open to create a multi-story vertical space, allowing light and air to flow through.

examples.japanese: このビルのロビーは{吹|ふ}き{抜|ぬ}けになっている。
examples.english: The lobby of this building has an atrium design.

examples.japanese: {吹|ふ}き{抜|ぬ}けのリビングは{開放感|かいほうかん}がある。
examples.english: A living room with a vaulted ceiling feels spacious.

examples.japanese: 2{階|かい}まで{吹|ふ}き{抜|ぬ}けの{家|いえ}に{住|す}んでいる。
examples.english: I live in a house with a two-story open ceiling.

notes:
ARCHITECTURAL CONTEXT: {吹|ふ}き{抜|ぬ}け designs are popular in modern Japanese homes and commercial buildings for creating a sense of openness and allowing natural light to penetrate deeper into the building.

RELATED ARCHITECTURAL TERMS:
・{天井|てんじょう} (ceiling)
・{開放感|かいほうかん} (sense of openness)
・{採光|さいこう} (natural lighting)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{吹|ふ}き{抜|ぬ}けの{玄関|げんかん} (entrance hall with atrium)
・{吹|ふ}き{抜|ぬ}け{構造|こうぞう} (atrium structure)
・{吹|ふ}き{抜|ぬ}け{空間|くうかん} (atrium space)

NOTE: The literal meaning is 'blown through' - referring to wind being able to pass through the open space.
